title: Privileged action write-log semantics and event context hierarchy
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Goal: Define a pragmatic, searchable, and privacy-conscious write-log semantics for privileged/administrative operations and a clear event context hierarchy so engineering, security, and product can rely on a stable audit dataset. This ticket focuses on what gets emitted at the point of admin actions (RBAC changes, SSO/SAML assertions, policy updates, invite/revoke flows), how differences are represented, and how contextual metadata (actor, target, session, assertion) is attached and indexed.

Background: Current audit streams are inconsistent across services: some emit full resource snapshots on update, others emit high-cardinality blobs. This has caused search, retention, and PII concerns. RBAC v2 rollout requires a reliable feed of admin events to support investigations, role lineage queries, automated revert playbooks, and downstream compliance exports.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: canonical event envelope shape, minimal required fields, op types for admin/privileged actions, compact change representations for updates, actor and target identification rules, contextual enrichment (SSO/SAML assertion metadata, session/IP), redaction guidelines, retention/aggregation tiers, and indexing recommendations.
- Out of scope: storage engine implementation, UI incident workflows, and full archival policy automation (these will be follow-ups).

Core proposals (high-level):
1) Event envelope: append-only JSON envelope with stable fields: event_id, occurred_at, service, op_type, resource_type, resource_id_hint, actor_type, actor_id, actor_identity_provider, outcome, client_ip, user_agent, request_id, request_path, session_id, saml_assertion_id (when present), before_compact, after_compact, change_ops, tags.
2) Op types: CREATE | UPDATE | DELETE | GRANT | REVOKE | AUTHZ_CHECK | TOKEN_ISSUE | SSO_ASSERTION | POLICY_ATTACH | POLICY_DETACH. Each event must include an outcome: SUCCESS | FAILURE | IGNORED.
3) Compact change representation: For UPDATEs prefer an ordered list of primitive field operations (path, op, old, new) where op is replace/add/remove. Example: [{"path":"/roles/3/members","op":"add","old":null,"new":"user:alice@example.com"}]. This keeps payloads small and avoids emitting full resource dumps by default.
4) Shallow vs full snapshots: Emit shallow compact diffs for high-frequency changes. Emit full-encrypted snapshots only when: a) the change affects policy or schema, or b) on explicit request (e.g., legal hold). Full snapshots should be stored separately (archival store) and linked by snapshot_id in the event.
5) Actor/target canonicalization:
   - Actor types: human_user | service_account | system_process | external_identity (SAML/OAuth).
   - Actor identity resolution must prefer internal_user_id if available, fall back to external_subject and idp. Include actor_confidence metadata with values: high|medium|low.
   - Targets must be typed (resource_type) and include a stable resource_id (if available) and a human-readable resource_name. For composite resources (role bindings), include a resource_path hint.
6) Context hierarchy and enrichment: Events should carry a minimal context and allow optional enrichment keys: session_id, auth_flow_id, saml_assertion_id, idp_issuer, idp_loa, client_ip, geo. The hierarchy is: request -> session -> assertion -> actor. Index request-level identifiers for fast joins (request_id, session_id).
7) Redaction and PII policy: Fields classified as PII (email, raw tokens, certificate blobs) must be redacted at emission time unless the producer service is explicitly authorized to record raw values. Redaction should use deterministic placeholders and keep a reversible mapping only in the secure archival store under strict access controls.
8) Sampling and aggregation: For noisy, high-volume admin events (e.g., autoscale authz checks), allow server-configured sampling with exact counters emitted (sample_rate, sampled_count) and maintain a small representative head of events for debugging.
9) Indexing & retention tiers:
   - Hot (30d): full index, searchable by request_id, actor_id, resource_type, op_type, outcome.
   - Warm (180d): limited index (actor_id, op_type, resource_type).
   - Cold/Archive (7y for compliance): snapshot links only; full snapshots retrievable on demand with authorized access.
10) Backwards compatibility: Provide a compatibility shim in the event consumer layer that can translate legacy 'payload' blobs into the compact diff representation when possible. Emit a version field on the envelope for future migrations.

Example event (compact):
{
  "event_id":"evt_20260228_0001",
  "occurred_at":"2026-02-28T15:12:03Z",
  "service":"identity-svc",
  "op_type":"GRANT",
  "resource_type":"role_binding",
  "resource_id_hint":"rb-84f2",
  "actor_type":"human_user",
  "actor_id":"u-1829",
  "actor_identity_provider":"okta:acme-inc",
  "outcome":"SUCCESS",
  "client_ip":"18.205.33.4",
  "request_id":"req-8a3",
  "session_id":"sess-993",
  "change_ops":[{"path":"/members","op":"add","old":null,"new":"user:alice@example.com"}]
}

Operational guidance and trade-offs:
- Storage vs search: Compact diffs keep storage and index size down. Some investigations require full snapshots; keep these as linkable artifacts.
- Index cardinality: Avoid indexing high-cardinality freeform fields (full emails) in hot indexes; instead index canonical ids. Use tokenization policies for search UX.
- Performance: Services should build diff payloads synchronously for admin APIs; background enrichment (geo, idp lookup) can be done asynchronously but must be attachable to the original event via request_id.
- Security: Request-level request_id must be unforgeable (signed by service) when crossing trust boundaries so downstream consumers can validate provenance.

Acceptance criteria (must have):
acceptance_criteria: Publish a canonical audit envelope JSON schema document in the security spec repo and link it from Console and Runtime docs.
Implement emission of compact change_ops for identity-service RBAC change endpoints (grant/revoke/update role) behind a feature flag.
Add actor canonicalization helper library (Go/TS) with clear fallbacks and actor_confidence semantics.
Define retention tiers and configure pipeline to enforce hot/warm/cold indexes with snapshot linking.
Create a migration plan and compatibility shim for consumers to parse both legacy payloads and new compact diffs.
Document redaction policy and require security approver sign-off before any service emits raw PII into the stream.
